title: Shrinebreaker - an online browser based 3-team retro spellcasting game
author: zrikz
selftext:
Shrinebreaker is a first-person team battle game for mages: three orders (Cinder Vow, Moon Veil and Reed Vigil) defend their shrines and fight over power pools in arenas, with retro painted fantasy art. It runs free in your browser, and there's an experimental Windows app. It's inspired by the 1990s online battle-mage games (Magestorm). I direct it, and Claude Code writes almost all of the code.

You can play it here: [https://shrinebreaker.com](https://shrinebreaker.com/)

This took roughly 5 weeks, but it's a little disingenuous to say this only took 5 weeks, as I've been working on a separate game for over a year and stole a lot of lessons learned from there, and a ton of the backend infrastructure support to greatly speed up the development efforts, but if I had to guess, this could likely be doable in \~8-10wks from scratch.. maybe?

  
Have had over 50 folks login and play, though concurrent user count has only been about 10 at the max. Would love more players to check it out!

**What the game is**

\- up to 3v3v3 teams of 33v33v33 team matches

\- Four disciplines (Elementalist, Mindweaver, Runewright and Warden) plus the Druid, a new class on public trial: roots, groves and spirit beasts from a wolf to a towering colossus, with 30 spells to level 30. There's also the rare all-spells Arch Magus.

\- Match types: Conquest, Two or three orders, Capture the flag, Free for all, Deathmatch, Escort and Warfront. Anyone can create a public or private match with bots, a level cap and bot levels.

\- Bots that fill the teams and play every discipline, so a match is never empty.

\- Progression: research picks in the Grimoire, quests with daily rerolls, feats, a 15-rank season pass with spell skins and new mages, guilds with guild chat and guild tournament nights, and a Hall of Honours.

\- Seasonal arena monsters: Halloween monsters, then harvest turkeys, a giant gobbler and pilgrim musketeers through November. More seasonal events to come!

\- A GPU renderer with a CPU fallback, three interface styles (the painted one, Modern and Hybrid), gamepad support and a Classic key layout. (Game works on any modern operating system / browser, including phones... phone experience is, passable.

\- **Discord authentication** \- you must have a discord account to play, I didn't want to deal with storage of username / passwords and discord has some good security / utilities built into it, so it was an easy thing to add on, especially with most gamers using discord anyways.

W**hat was done this week**

\- The Druid (trial). A whole new class with 30 spells, six spirit beasts, its own art and bots that play it. It went public for feedback, and within hours the first balance pass shipped, built from the live match stats and players' tickets.

\- Share your results. A Share button on the results screen: a picture of the scoreboard, a link to the full results, or a Discord post, now with personal bests.

\- Deathmatch in Create match, plus fairer quests: you only get quests for match types you can actually play.

\- Smoother big fights on crowded maps, adjustable gamepad dead zones, and a one-time tip when your browser has hardware acceleration off.

\- Fixes that came straight from players' in-game feedback tickets: casting while flying, invisible Druid bots, trapped spawns, and a stale cache that emptied the Druid's spell lists.

**Workflow**

Everything is built with Claude Code (Opus 5.5) on a Linux box that also hosts the live game.

\- One main Claude session as the producer. It triages players' in-game feedback tickets and chat, writes briefs, and starts background agents. Each agent works in its own git worktree and branch, writes tests, takes screenshots, and reports back. The main session reviews, merges and deploys, after the previous agents confirm on their own private test instance.

\- Deploy rules written down. Deploys go out only when nobody is online. Each one is checked by a Playwright run against the live site in four interface and screen combinations (painted and Modern, desktop and phone), and the update notes post to Discord.

\- Tests as the safety net. hundreds of test suites (\`npm run test:\*\`) cover the server, bots, movement, spells, renderers and UI, and every change adds its own.

\- Docs as memory. About 70 docs (decisions, protocol, balance, deployment), a running UPDATES log of every change, and Claude's own memory files for the owner's standing decisions.

\- Art from a second AI. Codex (GPT) makes the concept art and spell effects from briefs that Claude writes. Claude binds the art into the game and reviews it against the style guide, and I approve it.

\- Sounds / music - Turns out sound / spell effects are not easy! Hundreds of spell/music effects across all of the classes, and all were sourced from various places. Some were purchased from retail locations, IE Audio hero, BBC Sounds packs, others were generated across a few AI platforms, Elevenlabs for voice overs, Adobe Firefly for some effects, but I actually have had a lot of luck utilizing stable audio locally with my GPU - can generate 10 - 1 second clips in about 10-15 seconds; unfortunately the success rate is maybe 1 in 15, so many get trashed to find one - this is probably one of the most time consuming aspects, getting good sound listening to thousands of files to find what fits. I have had good success with Claude creating prompting guides for the various platforms though.

\-Players answered. Ticket submission is possible from in game for bugs and/or suggestions, and when a ticket's fix goes live, Claude writes the in-game reply to the player who reported it so the player can see ticket feedback, but then patch notes are posted for all to see as well.

\- The trailer was filmed by an agent. I know, it's not perfect, but.. trailers are hard too, so I used a Claude Code session on my Windows PC and it drove the game in a real GPU browser with Playwright, recorded shots through OBS, and cut the trailer with ffmpeg from a shot list and brief written by the server-side Claude. It filmed in private matches with bots, so no other players are on screen.
